entry.title: [UPDATED] GHSA-6973-8887-87ff: nimiq-block has skip block quorum bypass via out-of-range BitSet indices & u16 truncation
entry.content:
nimiq-block has skip block quorum bypass via out-of-range BitSet indices & u16 truncation

Aliases: CVE-2026-33471

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • nimiq-block — fixed in 1.7.2

### Impact `SkipBlockProof::verify` computes its quorum check using `BitSet.len()`, then iterates `BitSet` indices and casts each `usize` index to `u16` (`slot as u16`) for slot lookup. If an attacker can get a `SkipBlockProof` verified where `MultiSignature.signers` contains out-of-range indices spaced by 65536, these indices inflate `len()` but collide onto the same in-range `u16` slot during aggregation. This makes it possible for a malicious validator with far fewer than `2f+1` real signer slots to pass skip block proof verification by multiplying a single BLS signature by the same factor. ### Patches [The patch for this vulnerability](https://github.com/nimiq/core-rs-albatross/pull/3657) is included as part of [v1.3.0](https://github.com/nimiq/core-rs-albatross/releases/tag/v1.3.0).…

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0426: LLVM introduces timing-vulnerable optimizations into ML-KEM and ML-DSA operations intended to be constant-time
entry.content:
LLVM introduces timing-vulnerable optimizations into ML-KEM and ML-DSA operations intended to be constant-time

Aliases: GHSA-r7wm-4vf2-h44w

Affected:

  • orion — fixed in 0.17.16, 0.18.1

## Summary On targets that do not have a conditional move/select operations, LLVM compiles the internal `conditional_sub_u32()` function, into one that will contain a conditional jump on secret-dependent data, which could leak information about encapsulation and signing keys. `conditional_sub_u32()` is used throughout the field arithmetic of both ML-KEM and ML-DSA. ## Impact The variable-time jumps have been observed for ML-KEM and ML-DSA on: - `i586-unknown-linux-gnu` - `s390x-unknown-linux-gnu` Additionally, ML-DSA sees the vulnerable LLVM optimization on `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, for `hazardous::dsa::mldsa44` and `hazardous::dsa::mldsa87`. The leakage this LLVM optimization introduces could enable recovery of cryptographic secrets. The practicality of exploiting the leakage depe…

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0427: `sn-releases`: `extract_release_archive` writes archive entries without a path-traversal check (zip-slip)
entry.content:
`sn-releases`: `extract_release_archive` writes archive entries without a path-traversal check (zip-slip)

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

Affected:

  • sn-releases

`SafeReleaseRepoActions::extract_release_archive` builds each output path from the **raw archive entry name** and writes to it with no traversal check, so a malicious release archive can create directories and write files **outside** the destination directory, a "zip-slip" / path traversal (CWE-22 / CWE-23). In `src/lib.rs` (`extract_release_archive`, zip branch): ```rust let mut file = archive.by_index(i)?; let out_path = dest_dir_path.join(file.name()); // file.name() is the raw entry name if file.name().ends_with('/') { std::fs::create_dir_all(&out_path)?; // no `..` check } else { let mut outfile = std::fs::File::create(&out_path)?; // writes outside dest std::io::copy(&mut file, &mut outfile)?; } ``` The crate is unmaintained (latest release 0.3.1, 2024-10-…

  • https://crates.io/crates/sn-releases

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0428: BLAKE2b produces wrong tag when using `reset()` with a different-length key
entry.content:
BLAKE2b produces wrong tag when using `reset()` with a different-length key

Aliases: GHSA-xcc6-f2jq-43x6

Affected:

  • orion — fixed in 0.17.16, 0.18.1

## Summary `hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::reset()` does not correctly reset the state when a key is supplied that has a different length than the one used upon initialization with `hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::new()`, because it errorneously uses a cached length. ## Impact Initialization `hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b` with a key of some length `N`, followed by a reset with a key of length `!= N` will produce an incorrect BLAKE2b tag, causing `hazardous::mac::blake2b::Blake2b::verify()` to fail. This means under honest protocol conditions, parties could experience failing tag verifications. ## Resolution Upgrade to `v0.17.16` or `v0.18.1`.

References:

  • https://crates.io/crates/orion
  • https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0428.html

entry.title: [NEW] RUSTSEC-2026-0425: `nix-nar`: `Decoder::unpack` writes archive entries outside the destination directory (path traversal)
entry.content:
`nix-nar`: `Decoder::unpack` writes archive entries outside the destination directory (path traversal)

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N

Affected:

  • nix-nar — fixed in 0.6.0

`Decoder::unpack` does not safely contain the paths it extracts, so a malicious NAR archive can create files **outside** the destination directory — a path traversal (CWE-22). In `src/dec.rs` (`Decoder::unpack`): - A symlink entry's target is written without checking where it points (`src/dec.rs:153`), so the archive can create a symlink that escapes the destination directory. - The out-of-destination containment check compares path **strings** only and does not account for symlinks created earlier in the same unpack (`src/dec.rs:176-181`), before reaching the write sinks (`std::fs::create_dir` at `src/dec.rs:201` and `OpenOptions::open` at `src/dec.rs:218`). - The parser also accepts entry names containing `/` (`src/parser.rs:138-147`). Combined, a malicious archive can inc…

entry.title: [UPDATED] RUSTSEC-2026-0416: Stack overflow on deeply nested GraphQL documents
entry.content:
Stack overflow on deeply nested GraphQL documents

Aliases: GHSA-34cw-x8g7-rcv5

Severity: CVSS_V3: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H

Affected:

  • juniper — fixed in 0.17.2

The parser of `juniper` called itself once for each level of nesting in a GraphQL document. The parser had no limit on the nesting depth. Deeply nested selection sets, input values, and list types thus overflowed the stack of the thread that parsed the document. Validation and execution followed fragment spreads in the same recursive way. Long chains of fragment spreads thus overflowed the stack in validation and execution. A stack overflow aborts the whole process. One request can thus stop a server and drop all other requests in progress. The request needs no authentication. `juniper` 0.17.2 rejects documents that nest deeper than 64 levels or contain more than 15,000 tokens. `RootNode::limit_depth()` and `RootNode::limit_tokens()` change the limits.
